Rashi on Pesachim 72a:10:1.hebrew: את של ערב שבת בשבת - קסבור שהוא של שבת, וזה של ערב שבת היה אתמול חולה או שנאנס. ומילה שלא בזמנה אינה דוחה את השבת, דהואיל ועבר זמנה, ימתין עד למחר:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:10:1.english: The one of Shabbat eve on Shabbat - Thinking that he is [the baby] of Shabbat. And this [baby] of Shabbat eve was sick yesterday or was prevented [from being circumcised]; and a circumcision [performed] not at its [proper] time does not override Shabbat, for since its time has passed, he should wait until tomorrow.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:10:2.hebrew: ר' אליעזר מחייב חטאת - דלית ליה טועה בדבר מצוה ועשה מצוה פטור:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:10:2.english: Rabbi Eliezer deems [him] liable to [bring] a sin-offering - For he does not hold [that] one who errs in a mitzvah matter and performs a mitzvah is exempt.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:10:3.hebrew: ר' יהושע פוטר - דטעה בדבר מצוה ועשה מצוה, פטור; ואע"ג דחילל שבת ועשה שלא כדת, מכל מקום מצות מילה קיים. והכא נמי, אע"ג דאית להו קצבה, ליפטר, דמכל מקום עשה מצוה, דכל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן כשירין, וזה שמצא זבח אחד בעזרה ושחטו לשם תמידי ציבור, כשר לזבחו הראשון:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:10:3.english: Rabbi Yehoshua exempts [him] - For one who erred in a matter of a mitzvah and [nonetheless] performed a mitzvah is exempt; and even though he desecrated Shabbat and acted not in accordance with the law, nevertheless he fulfilled the mitzvah of circumcision. And here too, even though they have a fixed limit, he should be exempt, for nevertheless he performed a mitzvah — since all sacrifices that were slaughtered not for their own sake are valid, and this [person] who found a single sacrifice in the Temple courtyard and slaughtered it for the sake of the communal daily offerings, it is valid as its original sacrifice.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:11:1.hebrew: הכא במאי עסקינן כגון שקדם ומל את של ערב שבת בשבת - בשעה שמל את זה, עדיין שניהן עומדים, דמשום הכי פטור, דטרוד היה באחד מהן, דיודע הוא שהיום חובת האחד עליו. ומתני', כגון דקדים ושחטינהו לאימורי צבור, דהשתא לא הוה טרוד ועסוק בשחיטתן:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:11:1.english: With what are we dealing here? Where he first circumcised the [baby] of Shabbat eve on Shabbat - At the time he circumcised this one, both of them were still [there], so that because of this he is exempt, for he was preoccupied with one of them, since he knows that today the obligation of one [of them] is upon him. And [our] Mishnah [refers to a case] where he first slaughtered the communal offerings, so that now he was not preoccupied and engaged in slaughtering them.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:12:1.hebrew: ואע"ג כו' - בתמיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:12:1.english: And even though, etc. - [This is stated] as a question.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:12:2.english: [From Avel Arav] - Name of a place.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:12:3.hebrew: ושכח ומל את של ערב שבת בשבת דחייב - ואע"ג דעשה מצוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:12:3.english: And he forgot and circumcised the [child] of Shabbat eve on Shabbat, that he is liable - Even though he performed a mitzvah.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:13:1.hebrew: על מה נחלקו כו' - וקס"ד השתא: ברישא מחייב ר' מאיר כשמל את שניהם, ע"י [שסבור] ששניהן כבר הגיע זמנן, ומל של שבת תחלה, שזמנו היום, ואחר כך מל את של אתמול. ואף על גב דעשה מצוה, כיון דלא רמיא טירדא עליה בתר דמהליה לשל שבת, לאו טועה בדבר מצוה הוא. וסיפא פטור, משום דטריד בשל שבת והוחלף לו של מחר — דהא ודאי לא קאמר שמל את שניהם, דהא לא טעי בהכי. אלמא, היכא דלא טריד האידנא, לר"מ חייב:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:13:1.english: With regard to what did they disagree, etc. - And we currently assume: In the first clause, Rabbi Meir deems him liable when he circumcised both of them, because [he thought] that both of them had already reached their time, and he circumcised the [baby] of Shabbat first, whose time is today, and afterward he circumcised the [baby] of yesterday. And even though he performed a mitzvah, since no preoccupation rested upon him after he circumcised the [baby] of Shabbat, he is not [considered] one who erred in [the course of] a mitzvah. And [in] the latter clause, he is exempt because he was preoccupied with the [baby] of Shabbat and the [baby] of tomorrow was switched for him — for [there] it certainly does not mean that he circumcised both of them, as he would not err in such a way. Thus, wherever he is not currently preoccupied, according to Rabbi Meir he is liable.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:14:1.hebrew: ותסברא - דטעמא משום הכי הוא? השתא סיפא, דלא עבד מצוה דעדיין לא הגיע זמנו, פטור; רישא, דעבד מצוה, מחייב:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:14:1.english: And do you think - that the reason is because of this? Now, [in] the latter clause, where he did not perform a mitzvah — since its time had not yet arrived — he is exempt; [in] the first clause, where he performed a mitzvah, is he liable?

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:15:1.hebrew: אמרי דבי ר' ינאי רישא כגון - שנתחלף לו אתמול של שבת בערב שבת, ומלו בערב שבת, ועדיין לא נודע טעותו, וסבור שזה העומד של שבת הוא. ואע"ג דטריד ביה — דרמיא מצוה עליה כפי מחשבתו, וגם עשה מצוה — אפילו הכי חייב, משום דלא ניתנה שבת לידחות אצלו. וסיפא — ניתנה שבת לידחות אצל של שבת, וטעה בדבר מצוה, פטור; ואפילו לא עשה מצוה, לרבי מאיר פטור. והשוחט לשם אימורי צבור — ניתנה שבת לידחות אצל קרבן צבור, ואע"ג דקדים שחטינהו לאימורי צבור, הרי שכח; וע"י שטרוד בזבח זה בימים שעברו, ויודע שזבח זה עומד ליקרב, נבהל ושכח שכבר נשחטו אימורי צבור, ושחטן לשמן:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:15:1.english: [The Rabbis of] the school of Rabbi Yannai said: The first clause [is a case] where - yesterday [the baby] of Shabbat got switched for him with [the baby of] Shabbat eve, and he circumcised him on Shabbat eve, and his mistake was not yet known, and he thinks that this [baby] standing [before him] is the one of Shabbat. And even though he is preoccupied with it — for a mitzvah rests upon him according to his thought, and he also performed a mitzvah — nevertheless he is liable, because Shabbat does not stand to be overridden for him. And [in] the latter clause, Shabbat stands to be overridden for the [baby] of Shabbat, and [since] he erred in a matter of a mitzvah, he is exempt; even though he did not perform a mitzvah, according to Rabbi Meir he is exempt. And [regarding] one who slaughters for the sake of the communal sacrificial portions: Shabbat stands to be overridden for a communal offering, and even though they had already slaughtered the communal sacrificial portions earlier, he forgot; because he was preoccupied with this sacrifice during the past days and knows that this sacrifice stands to be offered, he became flustered and forgot that the communal sacrificial portions had already been slaughtered, and slaughtered them for their sake.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:1:1.english: If we say [we are dealing] with one who erred - [Meaning] he thought that it was a different offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:1:2.hebrew: שמעת מינה - מדקתני חייב, אלמא פסול הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:1:2.english: Learn from it - Since it teaches [that he is] liable, evidently it is disqualified.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:1:3.hebrew: עקירה בטעות - שלא נתכוון לעקור שם פסח ממנו, הויא עקירה כעוקר מדעת:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:1:3.english: Uprooting in error - [Meaning] that he did not intend to uproot the designation of a Paschal offering from it — it is [nonetheless considered] an uprooting, like one who uproots intentionally.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:2:1.hebrew: מה לי שאינן ראויין - עוקר לאו טועה בדבר מצוה הוא, ואמאי פטר ליה ר' יהושע בראויין? והלא לא טעה בו, שיודע שאינו פסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:2:1.english: What does it matter to me [whether] they are unfit - One who uproots [the original designation] is not one who errs in a matter of a mitzvah, and why does Rabbi Yehoshua exempt him in [the case of] fit [animals]? After all, he did not err regarding it, since he knows that it is not a Paschal offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:3:1.english: The first clause - [Refers to] the Paschal lamb that he slaughtered.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:3:2.english: The latter clause - [This refers to:] "And all other offerings."

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:4:2.hebrew: הא לא דמי - רישא לסיפא, דרישא בעוקר ולאו טועה הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:4:2.english: This does not resemble - The first clause [does not resemble] the latter clause, for the first clause is [referring to] one who uproots, and he is not one who errs.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:5:1.hebrew: לר"א - דדאין האי ק"ו, לא שאני ליה בין עוקר לטועה:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:5:1.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer - who expounds this a fortiori argument, there is no difference to him between one who uproots [the offering's designation] and one who errs.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:6:1.hebrew: ומקשי' ר' יהושע דשני ליה - לימא ליה דלא דמי טועה לעוקר, אמאי אהדר ליה טעמא משום ששינה בדבר האסור כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:6:1.english: And [the Gemara] asks: [According to] Rabbi Yehoshua, for whom there is a difference - Let him say to him [that] one who errs is not comparable to one who intentionally uproots [the offering's status]; why did he answer him [with] the reason "because he changed [it] for a forbidden thing," etc.?

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:8:1.hebrew: בפסח שאין לו קצבה - אין חשבון לפסחים, וזה שמצא טלה זה עומד בעזרה, כסבור שהוא אבוד מבעליו ושחטו לשם מי שהוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:8:1.english: With regard to the Paschal lamb, which does not have a limit - There is no [fixed] count for Paschal lambs, and this [person] who found this lamb standing in the Temple courtyard thought that it was lost from its owners and slaughtered it for the sake of whoever [owns it].

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:9:1.hebrew: תינוקות דיש להן קצבה - מי שיש לו שני תינוקות, אחד למול בשבת ואחד למול באחד בשבת, יודע הוא שאין לו למול בשבת אלא אחד:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:9:1.english: Babies, which have a limit - One who has two babies, one to circumcise on Shabbat and one to circumcise on Sunday, knows that he has only one to circumcise on Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 72a:9:2.hebrew: ושכח ומל את של אחר השבת בשבת חייב - דטעה בדבר מצוה ולא עשה מצוה הוא, דעדיין לא הגיע זמנו, ומודה רבי יהושע דחייב:
Rashi on Pesachim 72a:9:2.english: And he forgot and circumcised the one [to be circumcised] after Shabbat on Shabbat, he is liable - Because he [is one who] erred in a matter of a mitzvah and did not perform a mitzvah, since its time had not yet arrived, and Rabbi Yehoshua concedes that he is liable.

Tosafot on Pesachim 72a:15:1.hebrew: שקדם ומל של שבת בערב שבת - הוה מצי לפלוגי בדידי' בין קדם ומל ללא קדם, אלא דנקט רבותא בסיפא: דמל של אחר השבת בשבת — פטור, אע"ג דלא עשה מצוה, כיון שניתנה שבת לידחות. ורישא נמי קמ"ל רבותא: דנקט ע"ש, אף על גב דעשה מצוה — חייב, כיון שלא ניתנה שבת לידחות:
Tosafot on Pesachim 72a:15:1.english: Where he first circumcised [the baby] of Shabbat on Shabbat eve - [The Gemara] could have drawn the distinction within [that case] itself between [where] he first circumcised [him] and [where] he did not first [circumcise him]; rather, it chose [to teach] a novel point in the latter clause: that where he circumcised [the baby] of after Shabbat on Shabbat, he is exempt, even though he did not perform a mitzvah, since Shabbat stood to be overridden. And [in] the first clause as well, it teaches us a novel point: that it chose [the case of] Shabbat eve [to teach that] even though he performed a mitzvah, he is liable, since Shabbat did not stand to be overridden.

Tosafot on Pesachim 72a:1:1.hebrew: שמעת מינה עקירה בטעות הויא עקירה - אומר ר"י דפלוגתא היא בהתכלת (מנחות מט.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 72a:1:1.english: Learn from it [that] an erroneous uprooting constitutes uprooting - Rabbi Yitzchak says that it is a dispute in [the chapter entitled] Hatechelet (Menachot 49a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 72a:5:1.hebrew: הא לא דמי רישא בעוקר כו' - ומאי קאמר ר' יהושע: "שכן שינה שמו בדבר האסור"? אפילו שינה שמו לדבר המותר נמי חייב, כיון שהוא עיקר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 72a:5:1.english: "Surely they are not similar, [for] the first clause [refers] to one who uproots, etc." - And what does Rabbi Yehoshua mean [when he says], "for he changed its purpose to something forbidden"? Even if he changed its purpose to something permitted, he is also liable, since he is uprooting [its status].

Tosafot on Pesachim 72a:6:1.hebrew: לרבי יהושע דשני ליה לימא ליה הכי - תימה לרשב"א: הא אפי' אי מוקמי' כולה בטועה, ע"כ רבי יהושע לדבריו דרבי אליעזר קאמר; דלדידיה רישא, אפילו שינה לדבר המותר, חייב כיון דלא עשה מצוה — דמתני' מוקמי' בגמרא כרבי שמעון, דאית ליה היכא דלא עשה מצוה חייב לרבי יהושע, בפרק רבי אליעזר דמילה בסופו (שבת קלז.), דאמר רבי שמעון: "לא נחלקו רבי אליעזר ורבי יהושע על ב' תינוקות, אחד למול אחר השבת ואחד בשבת, ושכח ומל את של אחר השבת בשבת, דחייב משום דלא עשה מצוה". א"כ, מה שהוצרך לומר דרישא משום דשינה לדבר האסור, היינו לדברי רבי אליעזר, דלרבי אליעזר בסיפא נמי לא עשה מצוה, דפסל לעיל אחרים לשם פסח. ואומר ר"י: דבכמה מקומות מצי למימר "וליטעמיך" ולא קאמר. ועוד, דלא דמי לתינוקות: דהתם ודאי חייב כשמל של אחר השבת בשבת, לפי שלא עשה מצוה וגם לא ניתנה שבת לידחות אצל אותו תינוק; אבל פסח ששינה לדבר המותר — פטור, כיון שניתנה שבת לידחות אצל אותו פסח אם היה שוחטו לשמו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 72a:6:1.english: "According to Rabbi Yehoshua, for whom there is a difference, let him say to him thus" - Rashba finds this difficult: Even if we establish the entire [Mishnah] as [referring to] one who erred, perforce Rabbi Yehoshua is speaking according to the view of Rabbi Eliezer; for according to [Rabbi Yehoshua] himself, in the first clause, even if he changed [it] for something permitted, he would be liable since he did not perform a mitzvah — for we establish the Mishnah in the Gemara in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who holds that wherever one did not perform a mitzvah he is liable according to Rabbi Yehoshua, at the end of the chapter "Rabbi Eliezer d'Milah" (Shabbat 137a), where Rabbi Shimon says: "Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua did not disagree concerning two infants, one to be circumcised after Shabbat and one on Shabbat, and he forgot and circumcised the one of after Shabbat on Shabbat, that he is liable because he did not perform a mitzvah." If so, that which he needed to say that the first clause is [liable] because he changed [it] for something forbidden was [already] according to the words of Rabbi Eliezer, for according to Rabbi Eliezer, in the latter clause as well he did not perform a mitzvah, since above he disqualified other [offerings slaughtered] for the sake of a Pesach offering. And R"i says: In many places [the Gemara] could say "And according to your own reasoning," yet it does not say [it]. And furthermore, it is not comparable to [the case of] the infants: for there he is certainly liable when he circumcised the one of after Shabbat on Shabbat, because he did not perform a mitzvah and Shabbat was also not permitted to be overridden for that infant; whereas a Pesach offering that he changed for something permitted — he is exempt, since Shabbat was permitted to be overridden for that Pesach offering had he slaughtered it for its own sake.

Tosafot on Pesachim 72a:7:1.hebrew: לדידך לא אם אמרת בפסח כו' - תימה לרשב"א: מה משיב ר' יהושע לדברי ר' אליעזר "תאמר בזבחים ששינה שמן לדבר המותר"? כיון לר' אליעזר לא שני בין עוקר לטועה, מה מועיל מה ששינה לדבר המותר? הלא לר' יהושע עוקר לדבר המותר חייב, ה"ה טועה לר' אליעזר! ומפרש דה"ק ר' יהושע לר' אליעזר: נהי דלא שני לך בין עוקר לטועה, מ"מ יש לחלק, דרישא תרתי לגריעותא — עוקר ולדבר האסור, וסיפא תרתי לטיבותא — דטועה ולדבר המותר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 72a:7:1.english: According to you, no, if you say [that] regarding a Paschal lamb, etc. - This is perplexing to the Rashba: What is R. Yehoshua answering to the words of R. Eliezer, "[Can] you say [the same] regarding [other] offerings, that he changed their purpose for something permitted?" Since according to R. Eliezer there is no distinction between one who uproots [the designation intentionally] and one who errs, what does it help that he changed [their purpose] for something permitted? Behold, according to R. Yehoshua, one who uproots [the designation] for something permitted is liable, [and] the same applies to one who errs according to R. Eliezer! And [the Rashba] explains that this is what R. Yehoshua is saying to R. Eliezer: Granted that you do not distinguish between one who uproots and one who errs, nevertheless one can differentiate [between the two cases], for the first clause has two factors to [its] detriment — [he is] one who uproots and [it is] for something prohibited — whereas the latter clause has two factors in [its] favor — that [he is] one who errs and [it is] for something permitted.
